plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the two rotation operations on a binary search tree as a pair of small subtree drawings joined by dotted arrows. On the right, the upper node is a gray circle labeled x with a short stub edge rising to an unnamed parent; x's left edge ends at the Greek letter alpha, and its right edge descends to a second gray circle labeled y whose two edges end at beta and gamma. On the left stands the other configuration: y is now the upper node holding the parent stub, x is y's left child, and the edges terminate at alpha and beta below x and at gamma below y. Subtrees appear only as these labeled edges, without triangles. Between the drawings, an upper dotted arrow points leftward with "LEFT-ROTATE(T, x)" set above it, and a lower dotted arrow points rightward with "RIGHT-ROTATE(T, y)" set beneath it. Placing the before and after shapes side by side isolates what a rotation touches, the link joining x and y and which of them owns the middle subtree beta. The left-to-right order alpha, x, beta, y, gamma survives in both pictures, which is what makes the operation a legal local repair to the pointer structure.

interactionPlan.concept: A rotation is a constant-time pointer rearrangement that changes a binary search tree's shape — which of x and y is the parent, and who owns the middle subtree β — while preserving the inorder sequence α, x, β, y, γ.

demo_steps.title: The two shapes
demo_steps.narration: The same five items appear in two shapes: on the left y is on top with x as its left child; on the right x is on top with y as its right child. Only the x–y link and the owner of β differ.

demo_steps.title: Order is the invariant
demo_steps.narration: Turn on the inorder ribbon: both shapes read α, x, β, y, γ from left to right. Rotation is allowed precisely because this sequence is untouched.

demo_steps.title: β changes parents
demo_steps.narration: Step to the second assignment. β, which was y's left child, becomes x's right child — this is the only subtree that moves.

demo_steps.title: The parent link flips
demo_steps.narration: Next, y is attached where x used to hang on the unnamed parent. Forgetting this line is the classic bug: the rotated subtree floats free of the tree.

demo_steps.title: x descends
demo_steps.narration: Finally x becomes y's left child. Three assignments, constant time, no subtree ever traversed.

demo_steps.title: Run it backwards
demo_steps.narration: Switch to RIGHT-ROTATE(T, y) and step again: the identical three links are reassigned in mirror image, returning the original shape.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A rotation moves exactly one subtree — β — and flips one parent-child link, so the tree's shape changes in constant time while the inorder order α, x, β, y, γ stays exactly the same.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Two small subtrees side by side on a white background, joined by a central column of two dotted arrows. Nodes are light-gray filled circles with thin black outlines and italic serif letters (x, y); subtree names are bare italic Greek letters (α, β, γ) at the ends of plain edges, with no triangles. Each configuration's top node carries a short vertical stub edge rising off the top to an unnamed parent. Left drawing: y on top, x as left child, α and β under x, γ under y. Right drawing: x on top, α at left, y as right child, β and γ under y. Center: upper dotted arrow pointing left captioned LEFT-ROTATE(T, x) above it; lower dotted arrow pointing right captioned RIGHT-ROTATE(T, y) below it, both in small-caps serif. During execution, color the currently reassigned pointer red, ghost the previous position of β in gray, and tint the active node's outline. The optional inorder ribbon is a thin horizontal strip under each tree reading α x β y γ with tick marks aligning to the node/label x-positions. A small monospace trace panel to the side lists executed assignment lines, dimming lines not yet reached.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Code editor for tree rotation: learner completes LEFT-ROTATE(T, x) and RIGHT-ROTATE(T, y) by filling pointer-assignment lines for x, y, beta, and the parent link; Run animates the before/after trees and highlights every pointer that changed.

authoredContext: The search-tree operations TREE-INSERT and TREE-DELETE, when run on a redblack tree with n keys, take O.lg n/ time. Because they modify the tree, the result may violate the red-black properties enumerated in Section 13.1. To restore these properties, we must change the colors of some of the nodes in the tree and also change the pointer structure. We change the pointer structure through rotation, which is a local operation in a search tree that preserves the binary-search-tree property. Figure 13.2 shows the two kinds of rotations: left rotations and right rotations. When we do a left rotation on a node x, we assume that its right child y is not T:nil; x may be any node in the tree whose right child is not T:nil. The left rotation “pivots” around the link from x to y. It makes y the new root of the subtree, with x as y’s left child and y’s left child as x’s right child.

discrepancies: Scale/legibility: the 1260×455 viewBox is squeezed into the narrow area left of the docked UI panel, so the whole tree renders at ~40% size — node circles, the italic x/y glyphs and the small-caps Left-Rotate/Right-Rotate labels are far smaller relative to the frame than in the source, and a large band of vertical whitespace sits below the figure.

Node proportions: the source's gray circles are large relative to the edge lengths (radius ≈ half the horizontal child offset); the generated NR=36 circles against dx=100/78 spacing make the nodes read noticeably smaller and the Greek leaf glyphs comparatively larger than the source's balance.

The dotted transfer arrows are thinner/shorter relative to their captions than in the source, where the dotted rules span nearly the full gutter and the multi-chevron head is prominent; here the label typography dominates the rule.

Extra chrome not in the source (mono trace/pseudocode column at step>0, inorder ribbon, 'detached' annotations, violation rings) — correctly hidden at step 0, but they change the figure's look as soon as the user steps forward.
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful reproduction of the CLRS rotation figure (both shapes, parent stubs, gray circles, dotted bidirectional Left/Right-Rotate arrows) with an unusually rich and pedagogically sound interaction set (guided demo steps, direction toggle, frame scrubber/player, inorder ribbon, sandboxed code workbench); the main weakness is that the wide viewBox next to the tall docked UI renders everything small with a lot of dead vertical space, softening label legibility and node/edge proportions.
action_items: Shrink the viewBox (e.g. ~1260×340) or call setUiLayout to dock the controls at the bottom so the tree/arrow artwork fills the available width and the node glyphs and small-caps rotation labels render at comfortable inline size.

Increase node radius relative to edge length (or reduce dx/dy) so the gray circles read as large as in the source, and thicken the dotted transfer rules / lengthen them across the gutter to match the source's arrow weight.

Reduce the amount of default-visible auxiliary chrome once stepping begins (trace column, 'detached' text) or place it clearly outside the tree bounding boxes so it never collides with the α/β/γ leaf labels.
Collapse or compress the code-workbench section by default (accordion) so the first impression of the widget is the figure plus a few controls rather than a wall of UI.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; the issues are concrete rendering/layout fixes (viewBox sizing, UI docking, node radius, arrow weight, hiding extra chrome) that belong to the generator.

discrepancies: Overall art scale: the trees and the small-caps arrow captions render at roughly half the source's visual weight, leaving a large empty region below the figure; the source's large, bold display typography and chunky node circles read much stronger.

The two central dotted rules are shorter and the multi-chevron arrowheads are a rough approximation of the source's tapered triple-chevron heads (the outer chevrons sit detached and are of near-equal size).

During playback the 'live' panel (right panel for Left-Rotate) morphs in place into the y-on-top shape, so at the final step both panels show the same tree — the source's strict before/after pairing across the arrows is briefly lost.

Extra elements not in the source appear once stepping begins (pseudocode trace strip in the gutter, inorder ribbon, 'detached' annotations); acceptable pedagogically but they change the look away from the clean two-tree source once activated.
Node circles are drawn with a somewhat thinner stroke and the greek subtree letters sit closer to the parent circles than in the source, where α/β/γ hang at the far ends of long edges.
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful reproduction of the CLRS rotation figure (correct two tree shapes, correct arrow directions and small-caps Left/Right-Rotate labels) with an unusually rich and correct set of interactions (guided demo steps, direction toggle, frame scrubber/player, inorder ribbon, sandboxed code workbench); main weaknesses are the reduced visual scale/weight versus the bold source typography and the fact that the animated panel ends up duplicating the static panel's shape.
action_items: Increase the drawn scale (tighten the logical content box or enlarge node radii/font sizes) so the trees and the LEFT-ROTATE/RIGHT-ROTATE captions match the source's bold weight at inline size and fill more of the available canvas.
Refine the central arrows: lengthen the dotted rules to span the full gutter and shape the triple-chevron heads with the tapering/spacing of the source.
Consider keeping the source's before/after pairing intact — e.g. ghost or dim the static panel and label the live panel 'working copy' — so the final frame does not read as two identical trees.
Nudge α/β/γ labels further out along their edges and slightly increase node stroke width so the circles read as the source's heavy outlined nodes.

feedback.rationale: Concept, structure, and interaction design are correct (concept 5, no failure modes, no plan action items); remaining issues are implementation details like scale, arrowhead shaping, label placement, and panel state handling.

demo_steps.title: The two shapes
demo_steps.narration: The same five items appear in two shapes: on the left y is on top with x as its left child; on the right x is on top with y as its right child. Only the x–y link and the owner of β differ.

demo_steps.title: Order is the invariant
demo_steps.narration: Turn on the inorder ribbon: both shapes read α, x, β, y, γ from left to right. Rotation is allowed precisely because this sequence is untouched.

demo_steps.title: β changes parents
demo_steps.narration: Step to the second assignment. β, which was y's left child, becomes x's right child — this is the only subtree that moves.

demo_steps.title: The parent link flips
demo_steps.narration: Next, y is attached where x used to hang on the unnamed parent. Forgetting this line is the classic bug: the rotated subtree floats free of the tree.

demo_steps.title: x descends
demo_steps.narration: Finally x becomes y's left child. Three assignments, constant time, no subtree ever traversed.

demo_steps.title: Run it backwards
demo_steps.narration: Switch to RIGHT-ROTATE(T, y) and step again: the identical three links are reassigned in mirror image, returning the original shape.

plan.keyInsight: A rotation moves exactly one subtree — β — and flips one parent-child link, so the tree's shape changes in constant time while the inorder order α, x, β, y, γ stays exactly the same.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Two small subtrees side by side on a white background, joined by a central column of two dotted arrows. Nodes are light-gray filled circles with thin black outlines and italic serif letters (x, y); subtree names are bare italic Greek letters (α, β, γ) at the ends of plain edges, with no triangles. Each configuration's top node carries a short vertical stub edge rising off the top to an unnamed parent. Left drawing: y on top, x as left child, α and β under x, γ under y. Right drawing: x on top, α at left, y as right child, β and γ under y. Center: upper dotted arrow pointing left captioned LEFT-ROTATE(T, x) above it; lower dotted arrow pointing right captioned RIGHT-ROTATE(T, y) below it, both in small-caps serif. During execution, color the currently reassigned pointer red, ghost the previous position of β in gray, and tint the active node's outline. The optional inorder ribbon is a thin horizontal strip under each tree reading α x β y γ with tick marks aligning to the node/label x-positions. A small monospace trace panel to the side lists executed assignment lines, dimming lines not yet reached.
